name: service_monitoring
description: Monitor a web service and alert on failures

recovery_hints: Service may be down, check if the process is running
Check firewall rules and port bindings

example_params.content:
import subprocess
import time
import json
from datetime import datetime

SERVICES = [
    {"name": "api", "url": "https://example.com/health"},
]
LOG_FILE = "monitor.log"
CHECK_INTERVAL = 60

def check(service):
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["curl", "-s", "-o", "/dev/null", "-w", "%{http_code}", service["url"]],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10
        )
        return int(result.stdout.strip())
    except Exception:
        return 0

while True:
    for svc in SERVICES:
        code = check(svc)
        status = "UP" if 200 <= code < 300 else "DOWN"
        entry = f"{datetime.now().isoformat()} {svc['name']}: {status} (HTTP {code})"
        print(entry)
        with open(LOG_FILE, 'a') as f:
            f.write(entry + '\n')
    time.sleep(CHECK_INTERVAL)

steps.expected_outcome: Monitor running in background with PID shown

learning_signals: curl -w '%{http_code}' extracts the HTTP status code
nohup + & runs a process in background that survives terminal close
Monitor PID: use 'kill <pid>' to stop, 'ps aux | grep monitor' to find
